content: The CDC provides an SSGOV IND protocol for the treatment of specific filarial diseases, including lymphatic filariasis caused by infections with Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia malayi, or Brugia timori. The treatment regimen is as follows: Day 1: Administer 1 mg/kg orally after meals (PO PC). Day 2: Administer 1 mg/kg orally three times daily (PO TID). Day 3: Administer 1–2 mg/kg orally three times daily (PO TID). Days 4–14: Administer 6 mg/kg/day orally, divided into three doses daily (PO TID). For an extended protocol: Day 1: Administer 1 mg/kg orally after meals (PO PC). Day 2: Administer 1 mg/kg orally three times daily (PO TID). Day 3: Administer 1–2 mg/kg orally three times daily (PO TID). Days 4–21: Administer 9 mg/kg/day orally, divided into three doses daily (PO TID). For tropical pulmonary eosinophilia, refer to adult dosing guidelines. For visceral larva migrans, refer to adult dosing guidelines. Adverse Effects: Rare cases of encephalopathy. Fever. Gastrointestinal disturbances. Pregnancy and Lactation: Pregnancy Category X: This medication is contraindicated in pregnancy due to potential risks to the fetus. Lactation: It is unknown whether the drug is excreted in breast milk. Pharmacokinetics: Mechanism of Action: The drug exhibits both microfilaricidal and macrofilaricidal activity. Absorption: Readily absorbed. Distribution: Widely distributed throughout all body compartments, except adipose tissue. Half-life: Approximately 8 hours. Peak Plasma Time: 1–2 hours. Peak Plasma Concentration: For a 50 mg dose, the concentration ranges from 80–200 ng/mL. Metabolism: Metabolized to diethylcarbamazine N-oxide. Excretion: Primarily excreted via urine and feces.
